title: Minimum Space Standards for HDB Flats
what_it_is: Minimum Space Standards for HDB Flats

sections.label: HDB occupancy cap reduction
sections.summary: From 1 May 2018, the occupancy cap for 4-room and larger flats is reduced to six persons, aligning with private residential rules.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Currently, the cap is four persons for 1- and 2-room flats, six persons for 3-room flats, and nine persons for 4-room and larger flats.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: From 1 May 2018, the occupancy cap for 4-room and larger flats will be reduced to six persons, in line with the rule for private residential properties, and these rules are published on HDB InfoWeb.

sections.label: No cap on families together
sections.summary: There is presently no occupancy cap on families living together in their own HDB flats, which should apply similarly to single unwed parents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Then, surely, the same family cannot provide accommodation to their child or siblings who are single, unwed or divorced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: There is presently no occupancy cap on families living together in their own HDB flats and that should be the standard we apply similarly, whether or not it is a family or it is a single unwed parent.

sections.label: Published HDB flat sizes
sections.summary: HDB publishes the floor space for each flat typology, and families can choose which unit types to apply for.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: What we do for HDB flats is that we publish the size for the different flat typologies – 1-room, 2-room, 3-room, 4-room – all of different flat sizes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The floor space for each of these HDB unit types is made public and families can choose which ones they would like to apply for.

sections.label: Aligning HDB with URA standard
sections.summary: The HDB occupancy cap was 9-6-4, and Er Dr Lee advocated aligning it to the URA standard of six, which has been done.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: At that time, the HDB occupancy cap was still 9-6-4, but we had moved or we were planning to move it to six for private residential units.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And Er Dr Lee had passionately advocated for HDB to align its standards to the Urban Redevelopment Board (URA) standard, which is six, and this is what we have done.

sections.label: Purpose of occupancy standard
sections.summary: The occupancy standard applies for rental to minimise over-crowdedness and maintain the residential character of the HDB estate for families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The occupancy standard applies for rental and that standard applies really to minimise over-crowdedness and to maintain the residential character of the HDB estate as one meant primarily for families to live and stay in.

sections.label: Reviewing further modifications
sections.summary: The change was made to align with URA standards, and further modifications and enhancements will continue to be studied and reviewed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: As I have said, we have made this change to align with URA standards and we will continue to study and review if further modifications and enhancements are needed.
